ds: Payments or benefits offered to foreign public officials to obtain or retain business or an improper advantage, typically disguised as consultancy, marketing, or commission payments routed through third parties or offshore entities. Financial institutions see the flows as unusual payments to or from intermediaries, officials' relatives, or shell companies.

src.t: FATF, Specific Risk Factors in the Laundering of Proceeds of Corruption: Assistance to Reporting Institutions (2012)
OECD, Convention on Combating Bribery of Foreign Public Officials in International Business Transactions and related guidance
OECD, UNODC and World Bank, Anti-Corruption Ethics and Compliance Handbook for Business (2013)
Wolfsberg Group, Anti-Bribery and Corruption Compliance Programme Guidance (2017)

rat: Commission/consultancy payments to agents or shells for foreign official benefit via international wires.

ind.n: Success fee paid to consultant in a high-corruption market
ind.cx: Large success-based or commission payments to a consultant or agent tied to winning a contract with a state body in a high-corruption-risk jurisdiction.
ind.fp: Genuine commercial agents are commonly paid success fees; rates in some sectors are legitimately high.
ind.ds: Large success-based or commission payments to a consultant or agent tied to winning a contract with a state body in a high-corruption-risk jurisdiction.

ind.n: Payment to account in third country unrelated to services
ind.cx: Intermediary asks for payment to a bank account in a jurisdiction where neither the service nor the intermediary operates.
ind.fp: Treasury centralisation or tax-driven structures can place accounts in other countries.
ind.ds: Payments, counterparties or sales originate in or go to countries with no link to the customer, declared business, services or goods.
ind.cn: Payments or activity in jurisdictions unrelated to the customer's business or goods

ind.n: Intermediary shell with no operating footprint
ind.cx: Consultant is a recently formed company with no website, staff, or track record yet receives large fees from a firm bidding for government work.
ind.fp: Start-ups and sole-trader specialists may have a limited online presence.
ind.ds: Entity has no staff, premises, website or trading history consistent with its stated activity, yet receives significant payments.
ind.cn: Shell entity with no operating footprint

ind.n: Intermediary linked to a public official or relative
ind.cx: Agent or its owners are relatives, associates or former colleagues of an official with influence over the relevant decision.
ind.fp: Small markets mean many people have family ties to government; links alone are not wrongdoing.
ind.ds: Agent or its owners are relatives, associates or former colleagues of an official with influence over the relevant decision.

ind.cx: Invoices describe 'consulting', 'marketing support' or 'liaison services' without deliverables, timesheets or reports.
ind.fp: Early-stage or informal advisers may keep thin paperwork.
ind.ds: Invoices describe 'consulting', 'marketing support' or 'liaison services' without deliverables, timesheets or reports.

ind.n: Gifts, travel or hospitality for officials paid through third parties
ind.cx: Payments for luxury travel, tuition, medical treatment or property for officials or relatives, booked via a vendor or card.
ind.fp: Official delegations legitimately receive modest hospitality and reasonable travel for site visits.
ind.ds: Payments for luxury travel, tuition, medical treatment or property for officials or relatives, booked via a vendor or card.

ind.cx: Cluster of payments to an intermediary just before or after a tender decision, licence grant or regulatory approval.
ind.fp: Milestone payments often legitimately align with contract events.
ind.ds: Cluster of payments to an intermediary just before or after a tender decision, licence grant or regulatory approval.

ind.n: Round-sum payments split below approval limits
ind.cx: Payments to an intermediary are repeatedly broken into amounts just under internal authorisation thresholds.
ind.fp: Budget cycles and instalment schedules can create similar patterns.
ind.ds: Payments, claims or contracts are broken into amounts just under internal authorisation limits.
ind.cn: Payments or claims split to stay below internal approval limits

ctl.ds: Benchmarks agent commissions, rebates and fees, requires justification and compliance sign-off for payments in high-risk markets, and tests invoices for evidence of real services. It limits disguised bribery.
Monitors business partners after onboarding for adverse media, ownership change, enforcement action and conduct concerns. It keeps third-party risk assessments current between formal reviews.

ctl.n: Segregation of duties and dual authorisation
ctl.ds: Ensures no single person can create, approve and release a payment or master-data change, requiring an independent second approver. It controls insider and impersonation fraud.

Alerts on unusual countries, corridors, deposit locations and geolocation dispersion relative to the customer profile or on activity near designated risk regions. It focuses review on geographic anomalies.

ctl.n: Vendor master-data and bank-detail change control
ctl.ds: Requires independent verification and review of any new or changed supplier bank details before the next payment run, including challenge of redirections to third-country accounts. It stops payment-diversion and business-email-compromise fraud.

Identifies the natural persons who ultimately own or control a legal entity or arrangement and verifies them using independent registers and documents, looking through intermediate layers. It is the core defence against anonymity achieved through layered or opaque structures.
Risk-based vetting of intermediaries, brokers, partners and suppliers covering ownership, experience, references, public-official links and selection rationale. It limits exposure through proxies.

Requires declarations of conflicts from staff and third parties with annual refresh, rotation of relationship managers and challenge of exceptions. It reduces the chance that decisions are shaped by personal interest.

ctl.n: PEP, relative and close associate screening
ctl.ds: Screens customers, beneficial owners, controllers, counterparties and their relatives and close associates against politically exposed person data at onboarding and on an ongoing basis. Matches trigger enhanced measures and senior approval.
Requires logging, limits and pre-approval for gifts, hospitality and anything of value given to officials, with targeted audit of expenses and petty cash. It reduces improper inducements.

ctl.n: Lifestyle and high-value purchase consistency review
ctl.ds: Compares observed spending, luxury and asset purchases and personal-type use of business funds with documented income and wealth during periodic reviews and alerts. It highlights unexplained affluence that may indicate illicit income.

ctl.n: Cooling-off and delayed release for new payees
ctl.ds: Holds or delays the first large payment to a new payee or to changed details so the customer or institution can verify before funds leave. It buys time to detect coercion or fraud.

Tests bidding and award data for rotation, cover bids, price clustering, splitting, variations and exceptions to competition, and requires independent cost and justification review. It detects collusion and corrupt awards.
Tailors training content and frequency to role and risk for finance, relationship, underwriting and compliance staff, with feedback of quality assurance findings. It builds baseline competence.
Detects repeated transactions placed just below reporting or approval limits, tuned by band and window per segment. It counters deliberate splitting designed to avoid scrutiny.
